title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measures the marginal detection benefit of sandboxed emulation over a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility guidance into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are commonly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. In operational contexts, correctness and safety of generated artifacts are essential; a widely adopted mitigation pattern is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures. Prior surveys and system reports argue for workflow-centred mitigations but provide limited paired, cross-vendor quantitative estimates of the marginal value added by a guarded runtime stage [1], [2], [3].

Research question and contributions. Guided by a machine-readable preregistration, we ask: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) and its faithful execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full accounting of model calls and repair activity; (3) an interpretation grounded in validator coverage, task curation, and pipeline semantics explaining a near-zero marginal effect; and (4) reproducibility guidance and identified boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to add substantive value.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centric mitigations—pairing LLM generation with validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution—have been proposed across NetOps and adjacent domains to increase artifact correctness [1], [2], [3]. Empirical transfers from program verification and code-generation work show external verifiers often find errors that models alone miss, but gains vary with task type and verifier coverage [4], [5]. NetOps prototypes use emulators (Mininet, Batfish/NetKAT) and validator rule-sets to approximate production checks, yet systematic paired measurements of guarded-stage marginal benefits are scarce. Our study narrows that gap by measuring the guarded-minus-baseline paired detection rate under strict preregistered constraints and shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before execution (preregistration id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e; preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). The design is paired-binary: for each task the system produced one sampled initial candidate that both conditions analysed (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under this contract any between-condition discordance can only arise from (i) emulation observations not encoded as validator violations, or (ii) a permitted downstream repair-stage invocation.

Task bank, vendors, and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items came from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 synthetic family covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures invoked the preregistered deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds; irrecoverable failures excluded and deterministically replaced). In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model and sampling semantics. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We emphasise: temperature = null indicates the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; it does not imply deterministic sampling (temperature=0) nor provider-side determinism. Shared_initial_candidate was enforced: one sampled initial candidate per pair was reused by both baseline and guarded analyses and recorded in per-episode archives. Consequently, any between-condition difference is attributable solely to guarded-stage emulation observations or the allowed repair-stage invocation.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applying full intent-constraint validation (syntax, command ordering/workflow, required-field presence, policy-level constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by a sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against an emulated instance of the declared topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task; run accounting shows exactly one repair-stage call in the confirmatory execution.

Execution accounting and deterministic controls. The adapter family used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records model_calls_used = 721, completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0, and artifact hashes for primary result files. Deterministic reconciliation and provider_call_audit artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) document stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1. Contamination checks (artifact hashing, prompt-template checks, validator binary checks) were executed per the preregistration; no contamination flags occurred for the confirmatory set.

Scoring and analysis. Per-episode outcomes are binary: detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1} and detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}, evaluated with the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness handling followed complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs); sensitivity analyses treating irrecoverable failures as nondetections were preregistered but unnecessary because there were zero technical exclusions.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All values are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and the archived CSV artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution and explicit pointer. Run accounting shows a single repair-stage invocation and a single n10 discordant count. To enable independent verification we provide an explicit, archival pointer: the discordant episode is the unique record in the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1. Execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) contains the pair_id field for that record and the associated validator_trace and repair_provider_trace linking the guarded detection to the documented repair-stage call. Reproducibility steps: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha above) and locate the single record with baseline_score == 0 and guarded_score == 1; (2) read that JSON record's pair_id and inspect its validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields; (3) corroborate single-repair accounting via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json provider_call_audit (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1). These archival artifacts are authoritative and sufficient to reproduce the attribution without additional runs.

Representative diagnostics. Representative archived per-episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) include validator_trace objects with normalized_configuration, validation_before/after states, validator_version = 5.0, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count. Typical traces show the vast majority of shared_initial candidates had violation_count = 0 and that sandboxed emulation largely replicated validator findings—evidence of a validator ceiling effect for this curated task bank.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was applied deterministically. analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. No deviations affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log; contamination_summary.csv is empty for the confirmatory set.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors.

Validator ceiling effect. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic properties encoded in the synthetic task bank; baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111. Because the validator rule set covered the workflow patterns used by the task generator (shutdown‑configure‑restore, make-before-break switchover, paired MTU changes), there was little headroom for emulation to add additional detections.

Task curation and inclusion policy. Confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies rather than adversarially evade validator rules. This concentration inside the validator's expected envelope reduces runtime-only failure modes for the emulation to reveal.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The shared-initial design isolates guarded-stage contributions but removes between-condition generation variability; deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit record a single repair-stage invocation matching the single n10 discordant count. Thus the observed discordance is fully attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity recorded in run accounting rather than generation differences.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. The result implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs match its expected patterns (parser-validated, constrained intents), guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible aggregate detection value. This conclusion is conditional: in regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarially constructed inputs, stateful multi-step interactions, heterogeneous vendor behaviors, or validators with sparser coverage, guarded runtime checks and high-fidelity emulation remain likely to provide substantive benefit. The archived per-episode traces support targeted follow-up: (a) adversarial task injection is expected to increase n10 and widen the CI; (b) combining multiple complementary validator families could reduce the observed ceiling effect.

Statistical sensitivity and interpretation. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this as a near-zero aggregate finding is appropriate for the specific experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) but does not imply absence of practical benefit in other operational regimes.

Reproducibility and verification guidance. The execution bundle archives all key artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (manifest with preregistration SHA-256), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8), execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and representative scoring traces under execution/scoring/. For auditors: to verify the discordant pair and its repair-stage linkage, open execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha above), find the single record with baseline_score==0 and guarded_score==1, read its pair_id and trace fields, and confirm provider_call counts in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. These steps are sufficient to reproduce the principal attribution claims without rerunning experiments.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping via execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. We interpret the result as arising from a validator ceiling effect and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, complementary validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution summary (authoritative manifest): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts and provider_call_audit are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and produce a validator ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across model families and validator designs.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this constraint makes discordance sources downstream-only (emulation observations or repair calls).

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and stateful large-scale interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Residual provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain possible despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these uncertainties are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
